maria: Hey folks — opened a docs PR for the Console Observability page. Adds cost/latency breakdown section + a tiny tracing hook example. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/842 :wave:
aj: Thanks — quick skim looked good. Two nits: 1) the SDK snippet uses an old client name, 2) the link to the legacy dashboard migration page is 404.
ben: I can fix the client name. Which snippet do we want? Node and Python?
maria: Node + Python would be ideal. Keep them minimal — just enough for a user to copy/paste into a quickstart. Also add a one-line migration note for teams that renamed dashboards in v1->v2 (customers often search for "cost_overview").
olivia: Re: migration note — can we add the exact mapping table? e.g. cost_overview -> cost-breakdown-v2, latency_traces -> request-latency-panel. Even a short sentence in the doc helps.
ben: Yep. I'll add the mapping lines. Also AJ — can you confirm the API names for the SDK? I switched to `console.getCostBreakdown` but not 100% sure on param names.
aj: console.getCostBreakdown is correct. Params are start/end as ISO dates and groupBy: one of ["model","route","region"]. Example: groupBy: 'route' for per-endpoint costs.
maria: Perfect — Ben, can you drop in both snippets and update the link? Then ping docs-ci.
docs-ci-bot: PR #842 — build started (docs lint + linkcheck). See CI: https://ci.redwood-inference.internal/842 :robot_face:
ben: Pushing commit now with fixes and a short migration table. Also added a tiny tracing hook sample for the Console that shows injecting trace id into our logs.
olivia: Could you paste the tracing snippet here before merge? I want to double-check the formatting for the code block.
ben: Sure — Node example below:
```js
// Node: attach tracing id to console events
import Redwood from '@redwood-inference/sdk';
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY });
client.on('trace', (t) => {
  console.log(`[trace:${t.id}] route=${t.route} latency_ms=${t.latency}`);
});
// fetch cost breakdown
const resp = await client.console.getCostBreakdown({ start: '2026-01-01', end: '2026-01-31', groupBy: 'model' });
console.log(resp);
```
ben: And Python quick example:
```py
# Python: cost/latency call
from redwood import Redwood
client = Redwood(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_KEY'])
resp = client.console.get_cost_breakdown(start='2026-01-01', end='2026-01-31', group_by='route')
print(resp)
```
aj: That looks good. One tiny nit: Python method names are snake_case in our SDK, so get_cost_breakdown is correct. Confirmed.
maria: Amazing. After CI passes I'll do a final docs style pass (headings, TOC anchor). Can someone please add a short alert rule link? I put a TODO where we discuss setting up alerts on cost spikes.
olivia: I'll add a link to the alert example in ops/runbooks once this merges. Leave the TODO in for now with a link reference.

aj: Once CI green, let's squash and merge. Also FYI: When you add the migration mapping table, please mention the approximate date we shipped the v2 dashboard renames (2025-11) — users ask for shipment timing.
maria: Added the date note. Thanks everyone! :tada:
